VALIDATION

Validation gates

The pre-registered criteria that every strategy must clear to be ranked, with the failure mode each one is designed to catch.

Why gates are declared in advance

The gates below are registered before any strategy is evaluated. That ordering is the point: if the bar can move after the numbers are known, the exercise cannot distinguish skill from luck. Each gate names the specific failure mode it is designed to catch.

Gate register

Validation gates - 10 pre-registered criteria
IDGateCategoryWhat it requiresThresholdWhy it existsDependencyReference
G1Minimum sample sizesampleThe strategy must be evaluated on a pre-declared minimum number of independent betting decisions.n >= 300 settled decisionsBelow roughly 300 decisions a strategy cannot be distinguished from noise at conventional confidence levels, regardless of the headline return.nonerulebook ↗
G2Out-of-sample evaluation onlystatisticalAll reported performance must come from data that was not used to select, tune or modify the strategy.100% of reported results from a held-out periodIn-sample results measure how well a strategy fitted its own history, which is the definition of overfitting.nonerulebook ↗
G3Multiple-testing correctionstatisticalWhen many strategies are tested, the family-wise error rate must be controlled across the whole family, not per strategy.White's Reality Check or Benjamini-Hochberg FDR <= 0.05Testing dozens of strategies and reporting the winners guarantees an apparent edge even when none exists.nonerulebook ↗
G4Probability calibrationcalibrationStated probabilities must match observed frequencies, not merely be directionally correct.Brier score beats the base-rate model; calibration slope 0.9-1.1A strategy that is well ranked but badly calibrated will still lose money at real prices.nonerulebook ↗
G5Closing-line valuestatisticalThe strategy must beat the closing line, not merely beat the opening line or its own average price.Positive CLV over a rolling 100-decision windowBeating a stale price is an execution artefact. Beating the closing price is evidence of information the market does not have.nonerulebook ↗
G6Bankroll and drawdown limitsriskThe strategy must survive a defined adverse path without breaching the bankroll floor.Maximum drawdown <= 20%; no single decision risks > 2% of bankrollA positive-expectation strategy with an unacceptable drawdown profile will not be followed, and therefore will not compound.nonerulebook ↗
G7Correlation cap on combined legsriskMulti-leg structures must measure the dependence between legs and price them jointly.No two legs with |rho| >= 0.35 without a joint modelTreating correlated legs as independent is the most common way a parlay engine silently loses money.nonerulebook ↗
G8Stability across sub-periodsrobustnessThe edge must not depend on one season, one opponent class or one market regime.Positive in at least 3 of 4 rolling sub-periodsA single good regime is usually a coincidence, a rule change, or a market inefficiency that has already been arbitraged away.nonerulebook ↗
G9No lookahead or leakageconductEvery input used to make a decision must have been publicly available at decision time.Timestamp audit passes on 100% of decisionsThe single largest source of fake backtest performance is using information that was not knowable when the bet was placed.Requires a timestamped decision log with input as-of timestamps.rulebook ↗
G10Reproducible provenanceconductEvery published result must be regenerable from a pinned data snapshot and a versioned code revision.Run manifest published with each evaluationAn unreproducible result cannot be reviewed, and an unreviewable result cannot be trusted.nonerulebook ↗
